correctness.rationale: Point evaluations continuous when s>1/2, positive Fourier weights make Σ invertible; reproducing-kernel minimum H^s energy is vᵀΣ⁻¹v. For 0<s<1, subordination of κ²−∂² produces a positive off-diagonal jump kernel, so the min/max lattice energy inequality is strict for basis-data interpolants whose difference changes sign at two sample sites. The resulting inequality is precisely 2Q_ij<0. At s=1, the minimizer on each circular arc solves −f″+κ²f=0 and the arc Dirichlet energy has cross-term −κ/(π sinh κℓ), giving Q_ij=−κ/(2π)∑(sinh κℓ_a)⁻¹ on cycle-neighbors and zero elsewhere. Four-point DFT gives Q_13=[S_0⁻¹+S_2⁻¹−2S_1⁻¹]/16 and limit (2^(2s−1)−2)/[16(1−2^(−2s))ζ(2s)]>0 for every s>1. Independent four-site high-precision checks at s=.75,1,1.25,1.7,2.2 corroborate limits; finite truncation at s=1 is not claimed exact. All quantifiers are resolved analytically.

value.rationale: A universal sign boundary for inverses of an irregular sampled covariance identifies when all Gaussian partial correlations are positive versus when higher smoothness can create positive precision interactions; an exact Markov/local endpoint and a minimal explicit violation matter for Gaussian graphical inference and fractional Sobolev trace forms. This is not a numerical or normalization-only result.

final_claim: For s>1/2 the circular Fourier Matérn finite-sample precision has all off-diagonal entries nonpositive for every distinct finite site set and every κ>0 iff s≤1: strict negativity for 1/2<s<1; exactly cycle-neighbor couplings at s=1, and a positive opposite pair on a four-site equally spaced circle for every s>1 at small κ.
limitations: Applies to the Fourier-periodic one-dimensional covariance, s>1/2, κ>0, noiseless distinct samples; no higher-dimensional, noisy or general geodesic covariance extension.
